land.text: Shandong, where the Longshan was succeeded by the Yueshi culture: 'In the Shandong area, it followed the Longshan culture period (c. 2600-1900 BC)'

predecessors.note: The longshan-culture dossier dissolves at -1900 and lists yueshi-culture as the successor for Shandong (its dissolve event names erlitou-culture as the single counterpart, so the Shandong half has no matching event there). Eastern Henan and north Jiangsu are nobody's land in -1900 (the Longshan outer settlements were abandoned about -2000) and are taken here from nobody.

land.text: Shandong, where the Yueshi 'was later replaced by the Erligang culture'

successors.note: The page equates the replacement with the Erligang culture, whose own page dates it 'from approximately 1600 to 1400 BC' and lists the Yueshi among its predecessors; the page gives no date for Erligang's arrival in Shandong (Daxinzhuang in Jinan and Qianzhangda in Tengzhou are named as its 'first regional centers'). The shang-dynasty dossier (Cliopatria Shang, -1600 on the Henan Yellow River valley) has no gain in Shandong at -1500, so the hand-over is one-sided; flagged in notes.

correction.text: Shandong (core: the Tai-Yi Mountains region in central Shandong), eastern Henan and north Jiangsu: 'Yueshi culture sites have been found in Shandong, eastern Henan, and north Jiangsu province'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Yueshi row. The page (infobox 'c. 1900 - c. 1500 BC') gives no area and no map; it counts 'More than 340 Yueshi sites' in Shandong. Shape: all of Shandong (868 cells) plus a 120 km disc at Shangqiu (Panmiao, eastern Henan) and 100 km and 80 km discs at Xuzhou and Lianyungang for north Jiangsu, about 300,000 km2 (1,185 cells) by the gazetteer, the researcher's reading of 'eastern Henan' and 'north Jiangsu' as discs. The page says the Yueshi 'declined and retreated to the Shandong Peninsula in the east' as the Erligang state expanded but dates neither the decline nor the retreat, and dates the Panmiao component to c. 1900-1450 BC, so the full shape is kept to 1500 and the retreat is not drawn.

region.text: Shandong; the core is 'the Tai-Yi Mountains region in central Shandong'

ledger.note: 1900 BCE: the Yueshi culture replaces the Longshan in Shandong. 'In the Shandong area, it followed the Longshan culture period (c. 2600-1900 BC)'; the infobox gives 'c. 1900 - c. 1500 BC' and 'The Tai-Yi Mountains region in central Shandong is the core area of Yueshi.' The core is read as a Tai'an-Zibo area (disc around Mount Tai and Zibo); the shape starts on all of Shandong because the Longshan dossier hands over Shandong.

region.text: eastern Henan: Panmiao (Shangqiu) 'has a Yueshi culture component dating to the early Bronze Age period (c. 1900-1450 BC)'

ledger.note: 1900 BCE: the Yueshi reaches eastern Henan. The page gives the Yueshi sites in Shandong, 'eastern Henan', and north Jiangsu and dates the Panmiao component from c. 1900 BC, so the year is the page's and the 120 km disc around Shangqiu is the researcher's reading of 'eastern Henan'.

region.text: north Jiangsu: 'Yueshi culture sites have been found in Shandong, eastern Henan, and north Jiangsu province'

ledger.note: 1900 BCE: north Jiangsu is drawn Yueshi from the start. The page names north Jiangsu as a site area but dates no site there and gives no spread; the year is bridged from the culture's start date (page silent), and the Xuzhou and Lianyungang discs are the researcher's reading of 'north Jiangsu'.

region.text: the Yueshi land, which 'was later replaced by the Erligang culture'

ledger.note: 1500 BCE: the Yueshi culture ends, replaced by the Erligang culture. Infobox 'c. 1900 - c. 1500 BC', 'Followed by: Erligang culture'; the page does not date Erligang's arrival in Shandong and says only that the Yueshi 'retreated to the Shandong Peninsula in the east' as the Erligang state expanded. The Erligang page (infobox 'Preceded by: Erlitou culture, Yueshi culture, Xiaqiyuan culture') dates Erligang 'approximately 1600 to 1400 BC', so the two overlap by about a century.

certainty.note: A prehistoric culture known from its sites (more than 340 in Shandong); no frontier is documented and the eastern Henan and north Jiangsu limits are approximate discs.

sources.title: Yueshi culture
sources.note: Identity, dates c. 1900 - c. 1500 BC, range (Shandong, eastern Henan, north Jiangsu), core (Tai-Yi Mountains), Longshan predecessor, Erligang replacement, Panmiao component c. 1900-1450 BC; no area.

sources.title: Erligang culture
sources.note: Erligang dates (approximately 1600 to 1400 BC), range (North China Plain), 'Preceded by' list including the Yueshi; thin on Shandong: no mention of Shandong, Daxinzhuang or the Yueshi beyond the infobox.

notes:
Yueshi culture (c. 1900 - c. 1500 BC, Shandong), typed culture like its predecessor longshan-culture; Cliopatria has no row. Two pages opened (Yueshi culture, Erligang culture); no area on either, so the shape is the page's three provinces drawn as Shandong plus two discs (about 300,000 km2).

To settle: (1) The Yueshi 'declined and retreated to the Shandong Peninsula in the east' as Erligang expanded, but no page gives a year, and Panmiao in eastern Henan carries a Yueshi component to c. 1450 BC, so the retreat is not drawn; a later pass with a source on Erligang's Shandong centres (Daxinzhuang, Qianzhangda) could split the keyframe. (2) The hand-over at -1500 names shang-dynasty (the Erligang culture is identified with the Shang), but the shang-dynasty dossier (Cliopatria Shang from -1600 on the Henan Yellow River valley) holds no Shandong and records no matching gain; the Yueshi and Erligang also overlap about -1600..-1500 per the two pages' dates, so the overlap in eastern Henan needs a ruling or the size rule. (3) The longshan-culture dossier lists yueshi-culture as successor for Shandong but its single dissolve event names erlitou-culture; no edit made here. (4) The page's Dongyi identification ('Many Chinese archaeologists apply the historical name Dongyi to the archaeological Yueshi culture', disputed by Fang Hui) is a name, not a state, and no Dongyi dossier is proposed. (5) Native name 岳石文化 / Yuèshí wénhuà was not read from the page text returned and is the standard Chinese name. (6) Gazetteer names used (Shangqiu, Xuzhou, Lianyungang, Taian, Zibo) all resolve.
